title: Townhouse rezoning in Blair Creek subdivision
subtitle: Regional water capacity, street townhouse flexibility, affordability and Six Nations comments shaped questions on the Activa application.
overview: The Planning and Strategic Initiatives Committee held a short evening meeting with one public hearing item. It considered a zoning by-law amendment for three vacant blocks on Blair Creek Drive and Blair Valley Street, in the Stauffer Woods Harvest Park subdivision, put forward by Activa Holdings Inc. The committee recommended approving the amendment {{vote:m1}}.

The change adds site-specific rules for the blocks. It allows reduced lot widths on end units and townhouse blocks of six units instead of four. Staff described the proposal as low-rise street townhouses that fit good planning principles and provincial, regional and city policy. Staff said the Region has no objection, because the proposal does not raise the number of units already covered by the existing servicing agreement.

For residents, the recommendation would allow more modestly priced ownership housing in a growing neighbourhood. Council still needs to adopt the recommendation. The application does not include designated affordable units. Councillors also raised water conservation and the idea of reviewing the city-wide zoning by-law for similar requests.

decisions.item: Zoning amendment, Blair Creek Drive/Blair Valley Street
decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council approve the Activa Holdings Inc. zoning by-law amendment for Blocks 1-3, Plan 58M-672, as set out in report DSD-2026-103.

debate: On regional water capacity, a councillor asked about conservation measures. The applicant's planner said builders already use low-flow fixtures and high-efficiency appliances, and that further gains have largely levelled off. Grey water reuse is rare.

A councillor noted that Regional letters said the Region could not support approval at this time. Staff explained that the February letter referred to a separate application in the same subdivision, which is on hold. For this application, the Region updated its comments after reviewing the approved units in the existing servicing agreement. Staff said no holding provision was needed.

On Six Nations comments, the applicant said landscaping requests such as native planting could be considered, and that street trees in the subdivision are native. Requests about setbacks were outside this application. Planting on individual lots is up to homeowners.

On affordability, the applicant said the units are not designated affordable but are priced lower than other forms, and that street townhouses are selling well. The chair also asked the applicant to share the idea of lighter, reflective roofing with the client.

The chair noted that requests for reduced lot widths and larger townhouse blocks are recurring. Staff said they are reviewed case by case. The chair suggested the ongoing zoning by-law review could address them so fewer site-specific changes are needed.
